title: Advanced Imaging-Guided Standard Versus Dose-Intensified Radiation Therapy for the Treatment of Newly Diagnosed Glioblastoma, SAGA 2.0 Trial
official: Stereotactic Advanced-Imaging Guided Radiotherapy for Glioblastoma (SAGA 2.0)
summary:
This clinical trial studies how well advanced imaging-guided standard dose versus (vs.) dose-intensified radiation therapy (RT) and dose-intensified accelerated RT works in treating patients with newly diagnosed glioblastoma. Radiation therapy uses high energy x-rays, particles, or radioactive seeds to kill tumor cells and shrink tumors. During dose-intensified RT, a higher dose than normal of radiation therapy is delivered over 6 weeks. During dose-intensified accelerated RT, the higher dose of radiation therapy is delivered over a shorter amount of time (2 weeks) than normal (6 weeks). Patients also undergo an advanced brain imaging positron emission tomography (PET)/computed tomography (CT) scan (using a radioactive drug called either FET or FDOPA) prior to RT to that may help doctors better plan the treatment. Dose-intensified and dose-intensified accelerated radiation therapy may be effective in treating patients with newly diagnosed glioblastoma. Giving dose-intensified RT or dose-intensified accelerated RT guided by advanced imaging may work better than standard dose RT in treating patients with newly diagnosed glioblastoma.

IND Numbers: 61300, 140882, 176402, 154793, 167879

interventions.name: Dose-intensified Accelerated Photon Beam Radiation Therapy

criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Age ≥ 18 years
* Histological confirmation of glioblastoma (IDH-wildtype)
* Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) Performance Status (PS) ≤ 3 at baseline
* Provide written informed consent or have a Legally Authorized Representative (LAR) who is responsible for the care and well-being of the potential study participant, provide consent in accordance with ethical, regulatory, and institutional requirements
* Willing to return to enrolling institution for follow-up either in-person or by video visit (where indicated)

Exclusion Criteria:

* Known to be pregnant or nursing
* Unable to undergo MRI scans with contrast (such as patients with devices or metal in head that is MRI incompatible)
* Unable to undergo amino acid PET (FET or FDOPA) scan (such as allergy to the contrast/tracer, or technical or patient factors per the discretion of the treating physician)
* Prior radiation (including tile-based brachytherapy) or chemotherapy for glioblastoma (note: prior cancer diagnoses and treatment for other cancers are not exclusion criteria, and multiple surgeries prior to enrollment is not an exclusion criteria)
